info.title: Heist External API
info.description: Create an OAuth app in Settings → OAuth apps and send its access token in the Authorization: Bearer <token> header. Exchange the app's client ID and secret for access tokens at https://identity.heist.security/oauth2/token using the OAuth 2.0 client_credentials grant. Requests are scoped to the app's workspace and permissions.

oauth2.description: OAuth app client credentials. Authenticate to the token endpoint with HTTP Basic (client_secret_basic) or client_id and client_secret form fields (client_secret_post), then send the access token as a Bearer token.

post.description: Create a credential using an existing sign-in method. Provide its matching payload; GOOGLE needs none. BASIC supports existing username/password accounts: basic.username may be a customer-owned email address and basic.password is the account password. Heist cannot read emails sent to addresses outside tester.heisthq.com. EMAIL is for email OTP or magic-link login and requires a Heist-controlled address on tester.heisthq.com. MICROSOFT and CUSTOM use a generated Heist email. SMS and CUSTOM use an available Heist phone. Omit applicationIds to link all in-scope roots, or send [] to create unassigned. isCrossWorkspace creates a separate tenant lane; entityId joins an existing lane. New credentials are appended at the least privileged position; use reorder_application_credentials to change the order.

get.description: Get an available Heist email and SMS numbers for credential creation. email is null when all generated mailbox names are used; available SMS numbers are still returned. post.description: Test a credential's sign-in on an application it is linked to. Requires Editor or Admin and a plan that can run pentests. API key, HTTP basic, OAuth2 client credentials, static cookie and anonymous credentials are not tested. Returns 409 if this credential is already being tested on the application. Keep runId to read this attempt's outcome with get_credential_test.

401.description: Missing, invalid, expired, or revoked token

get.description: Read one credential test attempt by its runId. COMPLETED means sign-in succeeded. FAILED means the test did not confirm sign-in, which can also be caused by a test error rather than the credential; success is null while the test runs or if it was cancelled, terminated or timed out. Returns 404 once Temporal no longer retains the attempt.

post.description: Let Heist sign up for test accounts on an application and save them as credentials. Requires Editor or Admin and a plan that can run pentests. Choose a lane (PRIMARY, SECOND_TENANT or LOWER_PRIVILEGE) to register one account, or omit it to register all three. Optional instructions help the agent sign up. One signup runs per workspace at a time; returns 409 while another is running. Keep runId to read the accounts with get_credential_signup.

401.description: Missing, invalid, expired, or revoked token

get.description: Read one signup attempt by its runId. result is set once the run is COMPLETED and lists each lane's account; a completed run can still contain failed accounts. Read saved accounts with get_credential; passwords are never returned. Returns 404 once Temporal no longer retains the attempt.
